name: Guardian genius crossword No 221
preamble: Eight across solutions are one letter too long for their allotted space; these letters should be dropped to produce another word for entry in the grid. Eight down solutions are one letter too short and one of the above eight letters must added to produce a word for entry in the grid. The eight letters involved make an anagram for an appropriate word. Each of the remaining 16 clues contains a superfluous word (or words), which provide definitions for the 16 new solutions in the grid.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it or the preamble's rule (a letter dropped or added) makes of its answer, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: Most pale wine is swallowed by nuisance

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
a pest is an annoying person or thing

explanation.surface: Someone is looking very pale after a nuisance drank all the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to PASTIEST; as an across entry it drops a letter, T, to enter PASTIES, which the spare word 'pies' in 20 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty describes an unhealthily pallid complexion, and the superlative means palest of all.

clue.text: They build up bridge supports, crossing lake

indicators.note: a bridge crossing water spans it, so the supports straddle the single letter

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
piers are the pillars holding up a bridge

explanation.surface: Engineers building up a bridge put in supports across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to PILERS; as a down entry it gains F to enter PILFERS, which the spare word 'steals' in 15 Across defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A piler is one who piles things up, so pilers are people who build up heaps or stacks.

clue.text: Comic figure animated our quarantine sphere

indicators.note: animated means set moving, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 10 Across, ISOLATION
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cartoon hero comes to life to save a planet under lockdown.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'quarantine' set aside, OUR and SPHERE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero is a costumed figure with special powers, the staple of comic books.

clue.text: Being scrupulous in raising support for country

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word upward, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the spare words, ignored here; they define 4 Down, STICKLING
taken as written
aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Someone careful about fundraising support for a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Being scrupulous' set aside, IN is followed by AID written upwards, DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Bit of lint in cloth of mattress is irritating

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter
one thing sits inside another, so the letter goes within the fabric

blocks.note: the first letter of lint
ticking is the strong striped fabric used to cover mattresses

explanation.surface: A scrap of fluff caught in the mattress cover is annoying the sleeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to TICKLING; as a down entry it gains S to enter STICKLING, which the spare words 'Being scrupulous' in 3 Down define.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickling skin causes a prickly sensation, so tickling describes something irritating like a cough or itch.

clue.text: Cent to be plated with gold in bargain month

indicators.note: something plated is coated all round, so the metal wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cent
taken as written
or is gold in heraldry
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 23 Down, STEAL

explanation.surface: A penny coin is to be gold-plated as part of a monthly deal.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'bargain' set aside, C and TO BE sit inside OR, the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: October is the tenth calendar month of the year.

clue.text: Ragout, like eggs, beginning to offset emptiness

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: the spare word, ignored here; it defines 21 Across, SALMI
the first letter of offset
a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: A stew made with eggs, to help fill an empty stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Ragout' set aside, O from offset is followed by VOID.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, so it describes things shaped like eggs.

clue.text: Percussive sounds from a pair of pianos amidst bell sounds

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of, so the pieces go inside the ringing

blocks.note: taken as written
P is piano, soft in music, so two of them are PP
tings are the light ringing notes of a bell

explanation.surface: Drum-like noises from two pianos mingling with chiming bells.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to TAPPINGS; as a down entry it gains R to enter TRAPPINGS, which the spare words 'colourful clothes' in 12 Across define.
explanation.definitionFit: Tappings are light knocking noises, a kind of percussive sound.

clue.text: Last support that is to be pumped into old rail company

indicators.note: pumping something into a vessel puts it inside, so these letters go within the company

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
BR was British Rail, the former nationalised railway

explanation.surface: A final cash injection to prop up a failing railway firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to BIER; as a down entry it gains R to enter BRIER, which the spare word 'pipe' in 24 Down defines, a brier being a pipe of briar root.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the stand on which a coffin rests, the last support a person has.

clue.text: Family presented in newspaper as being dissolute

indicators.note: something presented in a paper appears inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: kin are relatives
a rag is a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid portrays a family as debauched.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to RAKING; as a down entry it gains N to enter RANKING, which the spare word 'Assessing' in 13 Across defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake is to live like a rake, a dissipated pleasure-seeker, so raking means leading a debauched life.

clue.text: Turned down work aboard sleigh

indicators.note: aboard means riding inside a vehicle, so the short word goes within the sledge

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
a sled is a sledge or sleigh

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a job working on Santa's sleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to SLOPED; as an across entry it drops S to enter LOPED, which the spare word 'Ran' in 27 Across defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that sloped was inclined, angled downwards like a hill.

clue.text: Tanning? Tan oil is on, smeared

indicators.note: something smeared is spread about out of shape, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sunbather asks about tanning while rubbing on oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to INSOLATION; as an across entry it drops N to enter ISOLATION, which the spare word 'quarantine' in 2 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolation is exposure to the sun's rays, which is how skin gets tanned; the question mark flags the loose example.

clue.text: Set aside weapon given to vessel in swirling dark river

indicators.note: given to means added on, so one piece is joined to the next
swirling water turns back on itself, so the river's name runs the other way
one thing placed in another goes inside it

blocks.note: an arm is a weapon
Noah's ark was a vessel
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 25 Across, LIGHTLESS
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A weapon is handed over to a boat on a dark swirling river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' is the spare word, not part of the river. The Dee is a river in Scotland, another flowing between Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means reserved or set apart for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Indian religious follower is to discuss returning colourful clothes

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to rap is to talk or chat
the spare words, ignored here; they define 6 Down, TRAPPINGS

explanation.walkthrough: With 'colourful clothes' set aside, IS RAP is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi is a member of the Zoroastrian community in India, descended from Persian refugees.

clue.text: Assessing part of opera as central in it

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside it

blocks.note: the spare word, ignored here; it defines 8 Down, RANKING

it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A critic judges which scene is the heart of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Assessing' set aside, CEN goes inside SA. 'It' as sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is an extended dramatic solo in an opera, a scene or section of the work.

clue.text: Believing that man is tenor featured in movement

indicators.note: something featured in a show appears within it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: he is a man, by pronoun
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tenor
a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: Someone believes a tenor is the star of the musical movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to THEISTIC; as a down entry it gains A to enter ATHEISTIC, which the spare word 'pagan' in 28 Across defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Theistic describes belief in a god or gods, so it means believing in religious terms.

clue.text: Scamp steals final thing in the immediate future

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a scamp
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 1 Down, PILFERS
an ending is the last part of something

explanation.surface: A young rascal will soon be pinching the last thing in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'steals' set aside, IMP is followed by ENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Impending means about to happen, imminent, due very soon.

clue.text: Had cut core of dissent repeatedly in school

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so only the middle letters of the word are kept
one thing placed in another goes inside it

blocks.note: the spare word, ignored here; it defines 19 Across, STEAK
the middle three letters of dissent, taken twice as repeatedly says
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A school stamped out dissent again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'cut' set aside, the core of dissent is used twice inside POD.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it, so possessed is the past tense equivalent of had.

clue.text: Adherent goes downhill — record held in University is restricted by Derrida's notion

indicators.note: something held in a thing is kept within it, so one word goes inside the other
being restricted means hemmed in all round, so these letters go inside the notion

blocks.note: the spare words, ignored here; they define 22 Down, LUGES
a log is a written record
the OU is Britain's Open University
idée is French for idea, and Derrida was a French philosopher

explanation.surface: A follower's fortunes slide as a university record is limited by a philosopher's theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes downhill' is the spare phrase. The Open University is the UK's distance-learning university, and naming the French thinker signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideologue is a committed adherent of a particular doctrine or ideology.

clue.text: Startled mouths gape, particularly after dismissing University's brief comments

indicators.note: dismissing sends one letter away, so it is removed from the fodder
startled means thrown into disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 23 Across, SPECIALLY
U is the abbreviation for university, the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Students gape in astonishment after a university sacks staff over their short remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'particularly' set aside, U is taken out of MOUTHS GAPE and the rest rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Apothegms are terse, pithy sayings, a kind of short comment or maxim.

clue.text: Rebellious son, sailor, almost — almost — ruined bay

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the next word loses its final letter
something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the shortened word is rearranged

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
the second instance taken as written, to be shortened
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 26 Across, BIGHT

explanation.surface: A wayward lad and a sailor nearly wreck a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'bay' set aside, AB is followed by ALMOST cut short and rearranged; the first 'almost' is the instruction, the second the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Absalom was King David's son in the Bible who led a revolt against his father.

clue.text: About to enter bet, but not last — successful run?

not last means the final letter is left off

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a stake is a wager

explanation.surface: A gambler is about to place a bet, hoping for a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to STREAK; as an across entry it drops R to enter STEAK, which the spare word 'cut' in 16 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is an unbroken series, as in a winning streak, a successful run.

clue.text: Home for 2 ornate tiny pork pies, not one

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 1 Across, PASTIES

explanation.surface: A fancy home features dainty pork pies.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'pies' set aside, I (one) is removed from TINY PORK and the rest rearranged. 2 points to 2 Down, SUPERHERO: Superman came from Krypton.
explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is the fictional planet where Superman was born, the home of that comic hero.

clue.text: Spoke endlessly about reduced meat in sausage

reduced means made shorter, so the word is cut back by its last letter
about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: said is spoke, in the past tense
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: Someone went on and on about the scant meat in a banger.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to SALAMI; as an across entry it drops A to enter SALMI, which the spare word 'Ragout' in 5 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a highly seasoned cured sausage of Italian origin.

clue.text: Bullets missing head? Clumsy fools

blocks.note: slugs are bullets in slang

explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to LUGS; as a down entry it gains E to enter LUGES, which the spare words 'goes downhill' in 17 Down define.
explanation.definitionFit: A lug is a slang term for a big, awkward, dim-witted man, a clumsy oaf.

clue.text: Pieces reassembled by collaborator, chiefly

blocks.note: taken as written
an ally works alongside one, a collaborator

explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to ESPECIALLY; as an across entry it drops E to enter SPECIALLY, which the spare word 'particularly' in 18 Across defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Especially means above all, principally, just as chiefly does.

clue.text: Nurse alone can provide confirmation

indicators.note: the words supply the answer from within their own letters

blocks.note: found inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A nurse working solo is able to give the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to SEAL; as a down entry it gains T to enter STEAL, which the spare word 'bargain' in 5 Across defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a mark of approval or authentication, as in seal of approval, so it is confirmation.

clue.text: Lodge pipe, black, running into one sea

indicators.note: running into something takes you inside it

blocks.note: the spare word, ignored here; it defines 7 Down, BRIER
I is the Roman numeral one
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.walkthrough: With 'pipe' set aside, B goes inside MED, after I.

explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a bird that cannot fly, so flightless describes it; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Colourful sailing ship heads for home today

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

blocks.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
the first letters of home and today

explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to BRIGHT; as an across entry it drops R to enter BIGHT, which the spare word 'bay' in 18 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright colours are vivid ones, so bright means colourful.

clue.text: Ran theatre production — returned amount I reckon should be reduced

taken as written

clue.text: Poor information about old pagan produces resentment

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a dud is something useless, poor

the spare word, ignored here; it defines 14 Down, ATHEISTIC
